objections.claim: The count-pinned three-member consumption rule is a RULE-GOVERNED restatement and an item becomes live work through exactly one listed carrier.
objections.evidence: The count of written members is three, but the set is neither exhaustive nor exclusive. D-001 section 3 names Route A, a V1 successor through the coop process, as a lawful route; D-017 omits it. Conversely, D-001's condition-2 MF-6/new-row rule requires a register-content decision to receive D-000 review and then amend file 08, so D-017 members 1 and 2 normally co-occur. D-018 itself says each future Route B disposition is an isolated reviewed entry, so members 1 and 3 also co-occur. D-017 section 5 reinforces the contradiction by requiring a promoted register gap to have its own D-000 entry. The new exclusivity rule and one-entry-per-promotion granularity are therefore not mere restatements of the cited bytes, making the RULE-GOVERNED classification false as drafted.
objections.proposedFix: Replace 'exactly one of' with the applicable, potentially combined authority path and include Route A explicitly. State that a D-000 decision may be recorded together with its file-08 amendment and that a Route B disposition may itself be a D-000-reviewed entry. Either narrow D-017 to the already-recorded authority hierarchy or isolate and mark the novel routing/granularity choice PREFERENCE-LADEN.

objections.claim: Changing a count-pinned enumeration 're-opens this row.'
objections.evidence: D-017 and D-018 would be coordinator decision entries, not rows in file 08. The coordinator register's closed status vocabulary is ADOPTED, CONTESTED, SUPERSEDED, and OVERTURNED; it has no re-opened state. Using row/re-open language while D-017 declares file 08 the sole checklist creates an undefined shadow status surface. The defect appears once in D-017 and twice in D-018.
objections.proposedFix: Say that changing a count-pinned enumeration requires a separately reviewed successor or supersession of the decision. Reserve row status and re-opening language for actual file-08 rows whose status rule defines it.

objections.claim: Preview naming, four-row Route B selection, and the seven-step execution order form one reversible preference-laden decision.
objections.evidence: They are three independently contestable acts: the D-002 slice can be called a preview while Route A remains selected; Route B can be selected without adopting this execution order; and the order can change without renaming the slice. D-000 clause 4 requires commit/push per decision and clause 5 requires a cheaper overturn for preference-laden choices. One C-D018 revert cannot overturn any one of these acts without overturning the other two. D-016 records this exact defect class: bundling a preference-laden carrier choice inside another decision made its apparent overturn procedure formal rather than real. D-018's own dependent-entry caveat addresses later commits, not the three sibling choices already bundled inside C-D018.
objections.proposedFix: Split at least (a) preview/MVP naming, (b) Route B selection, and (c) execution sequencing into separately reviewed entries and commits. Also make the four per-row Route B selections explicitly severable, or justify and encode why they must rise and fall together; later disposition artifacts remain separate in either case.

objections.claim: The selected four-row Route B path lets preview design avoid serialization behind TM-complete closure while DR-003 is not waived and only a scoped preview threat model remains required.
objections.evidence: D-001's route for DR-003 is Route A and states that applying v10-disposition is necessary but insufficient: closure also requires the V10/custody plus G19 demonstration and TM's final disposition. D-001 condition 1 still requires DR-003 to be SATISFIED or to receive its own explicit scoped reviewed pre-blueprint disposition. D-018's count-pinned Route B set excludes DR-003. Merely saying a scoped threat model remains required is not such a disposition. Therefore the preview remains blocked on full DR-003 Route A closure, including much of the same V10/custody/G19 work D-018 claims Route B avoids; the trade paragraph's claimed gain is false on the selected set.
objections.proposedFix: Choose explicitly between two honest paths: select and separately review a scoped Route B disposition for DR-003 while retaining a real preview threat model, or leave DR-003 on Route A and remove every claim that the preview is no longer serialized behind TM-complete/V10-custody/G19 closure. Do not describe a required scoped threat model as if it already satisfies condition 1.

objections.claim: Authoritative-MVP Route A work is not deprioritized by the adopted seven-step sequence.
objections.evidence: The operative sequence schedules isolated preview/product decisions, register mechanics, selected live defects, four preview Route B dispositions, and preview product contracts in steps 1 through 5. Step 6 is conditional recalculation. General execution of file 08, where the named identity, D9, Phase-1A, evidence/retention, and V10/custody/G19 Route A work lives, is deferred to step 7. Section 5 says those streams remain owned, but the sequence gives them no parallel start, owner, or milestone. The evidence-head repair in step 3 is not the full set claimed in section 5. Thus 'not deprioritized' is a disclosed caveat contradicted by the adopted order.
objections.proposedFix: Add an explicit Route A lane that starts in parallel with the preview decisions and name its owners/milestones, or remove the non-deprioritization claim and record the actual preference trade. The sequence must state that steps 4 and 5 do not gate continued Route A work if that is the intended decision.

objections.claim: Route B 'authorizes at most a preview blueprint under D-001 condition 5.'
objections.evidence: D-001 defines Route B only as an alternative way to disposition a condition-1 row. Condition 5 separately requires product and architecture authorities to authorize creation of docs/v2/implementation against a refreshed exact authority baseline. D-018's readiness-effect paragraph correctly says condition 5 is untouched, so its earlier authorization sentence attributes power to Route B that Route B does not possess even though the surrounding caveats prevent an immediate status move.
objections.proposedFix: State that completed Route B dispositions may satisfy the scoped condition-1 prerequisite for a preview; they authorize no blueprint. Attribute blueprint authorization exclusively to the separate condition-5 act after all five conditions hold.
